title: 1997 AHSME Problem 28
statement: How many ordered triples of integers \((a,b,c)\) satisfy \[ \begin{aligned} |a+b|+c&=19,\\ ab+|c|&=97? \end{aligned} \]

solutions.text: If \(c\ge0,\) substitution and factoring lead to no pair consistent with the required sign of \(a+b.\) Thus \(c\lt0,\) so \(s\gt19\) and \(ab+s=116.\) If \(a+b=s,\) then \((a+1)(b+1)=117,\) producing the unordered pairs \(\{0,116\},\) \(\{2,38\},\) \(\{8,12\}.\) If \(a+b=-s,\) then \((a-1)(b-1)=117,\) producing \(\{-116,0\},\) \(\{-38,-2\},\) \(\{-12,-8\}.\) Each unordered pair has two orders, giving \(6\cdot2=12\) triples. The correct answer is E.
hints: Set \(s=|a+b|\), so \(c=19-s\), and split according to the sign of \(c\)
When \(c\lt0\), rewrite the resulting equations as products equal to \(117\)
